description.text: Align Technology, Inc. (“we,” “us,” “our,” “Align” or the “Company”) is a global medical device company primarily engaged in the design, manufacture and marketing of Invisalign® clear aligners for the treatment of malocclusions, or the misalignment of teeth, by orthodontists and general dental practitioners (“GPs”), ViveraTM retainers for retention, iTeroTM intraoral scanners and services for dentistry, and exocadTM computer-aided design and computer-aided manufacturing (“CAD/CAM”) software for dental laboratories and dental practitioners. Our vision and strategy is to revolutionize orthodontic and restorative dentistry through digital treatment planning and implementation using the AlignTM Digital Platform, an integrated suite of proprietary technologies and services designed to deliver a seamless, end-to-end solution for patients, consumers, orthodontists, GPs and lab partners. We strive to achieve our vision and strategy through key objectives made possible with the proprietary technologies and services of the AlignTM Digital Platform to establish: clear aligners as the principal solution for the treatment of malocclusions with the Invisalign System as the treatment solution of choice by orthodontists, GPs and patients globally, our iTero intraoral scanners as the preferred scanning technology for digital dental scans and our exocad CAD/CAM software as the dental restorative solution of choice for dental labs.

about.description_short: Align Technology designs and manufactures the Invisalign System, the most advanced clear aligner system in the world, iTero intraoral scanners and services, and exocad CAD/CAM software. These technology building blocks enable enhanced digital orthodontic and restorative workflows to improve patient outcomes and practice efficiencies for over 302 thousand doctor customers and are key to accessing Align's 600 million consumer market opportunity worldwide. Over the past 29 years, Align has helped doctors treat approximately 23.5 million patients with the Invisalign System and is driving the evolution in digital dentistry through the Align Digital Platform, our integrated suite of unique, proprietary technologies and services delivered as a seamless, end-to-end solution for patients and consumers, orthodontists and GP dentists, and lab/partners. Visit www.aligntech.com for more information.

employees.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 20,290 employees, a decrease of approximately 3.1% and 6.1% over December 31, 2024, and December 31, 2023, respectively.

analysis_md:
# ALGN — Align Technology, Inc.
Engine 5.5 pass-1 run, 2026-10-19. In scope (market cap $10.816B at $149.00, nasdaq_quote_api).

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, or ttm.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
Maker of Invisalign clear aligners, iTero intraoral scanners, and the ClinCheck / Align Digital Platform software workflow for orthodontists and GP dentists. Two segments in substance: Clear Aligner (Q2 2026 revenue $870.9M of $1,056.2M total, per the Q2 2026 earnings reports) and Systems & Services (iTero scanners and services). Demand is consumer-discretionary and largely out-of-pocket.

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** operating cash flow $593,223,000; capex $102,445,000 (rollup: PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment, key_numbers.md); SBC $185,870,000 (always a real cost).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $304,908,000 = $4.20/share** (key_numbers.md: latest FY OE total $304.9M, latest FY OE/share $4.20)
- Maintenance version (NI + D&A − min(capex, D&A) − ΔNWC): $354,230,000 — same ballpark; the FY2025 conservative figure was held down by a working-capital build (ΔNWC $191,112,000 in the CSV) rather than by operations.
- OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years. Balance sheet: cash $1,094,908,000 and **no borrowings filed in any year of the history** (see DEBT_TAGS_BLANK below); operating lease liabilities $114,446,000; equity $4,049,147,000 (all FY2025, financials_history.csv). Buybacks continue: $465,939,000 in FY2025 (fundamentals.json).
- The recent history is a stall, not a collapse: revenue $3,952,584,000 (FY2021) → $3,734,635,000 (FY2022) → $3,862,260,000 (FY2023) → $3,999,012,000 (FY2024) → $4,034,964,000 (FY2025). Latest rev YoY is 0.90% (key_numbers.md).

**Base used = TTM owner's earnings through Q2 2026, from ttm.py (filing-direct, no hand math):**
- OCF: FY $593,223,000 − prior YTD $181,326,000 + current YTD $343,799,000 = **TTM $755,696,000**
- Capex: FY $102,445,000 − prior YTD $46,768,000 + current YTD $66,450,000 = **TTM $122,127,000**
- SBC: FY $185,870,000 − prior YTD $93,205,000 + current YTD $86,484,000 = **TTM $179,149,000**
- Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **71,629,000**
- **TTM OE total $454,420,000 → base OE/share $6.34** (base_source: ttm_json)
- The engine's normalized base (3-yr median) is $5.93/share. The TTM base is used because the FY2025 figure ($4.20) is depressed by the working-capital build above and H1 2026 operating cash flow recovered sharply ($343,799,000 vs $181,326,000 in H1 2025); the TTM base is the fresher, filing-derived figure. The method range between the two bases is narrow (see Thoughts).

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate / narrow
Justification: brand, doctor network and the iTero/ClinCheck digital workflow give real switching costs and ROIC has stayed at 13-17% through a four-year revenue stall, but expired core patents, credible lower-priced rivals (Angelalign above all), flat-to-down guided ASP and a 7-point gross-margin slide since FY2021 cap it at narrow/moderate.
- FOR: Invisalign brand plus the largest clear-aligner installed base — a record 89,200 doctors submitted cases in Q2 2026; iTero scanner installed base + ClinCheck treatment-planning workflow create real switching costs for practices; scale manufacturing and SmartTrack material know-how keep gross margin near 70% despite competition; ROIC stayed above the cost of capital through the post-2021 stall: 29.5% (FY2021), 14.6%, 16.6%, 15.0%, 13.0% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json roic_proxy.
- AGAINST: Core Invisalign patents have expired — Angelalign, Dentsply/SureSmile, Straumann/ClearCorrect and Ormco Spark compete on price; pricing power fading: FY2026 guide has clear-aligner ASP flat to slightly down, with mix shifting to lower-priced products and countries; gross margin eroded from 74.3% (FY2021) to 67.2% (FY2025) in fundamentals.json; revenue has stalled since the FY2021 peak ($3.95B to $4.03B over four years, FY2026 guided +3-4%); consumer-discretionary, out-of-pocket demand — North America is only stable, not growing.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.
- Note on the moat evidence: ROIC of 13.0-16.6% in FY2022-25 is above a normal cost of capital but falling, and gross margin fell every year from FY2021 to FY2025 (74.3% → 70.5% → 70.1% → 70.0% → 67.2%, fundamentals.json). That is a franchise being competed down, not a widening one — hence 5, not 7.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check (mandatory): the engine's blended growth is 4.30% (components: rev CAGR 5y 10.30%, rev CAGR 3y 2.61%, latest rev YoY 0.90%, OE/share CAGR 2y -15.83%; share-count adjustment +2.54pp on the revenue components). Actual recent prints: FY2025 revenue +0.90%, Q2 2026 revenue +4.3% YoY with record clear-aligner shipments of 691.8 thousand cases (+7.4%), and management's FY2026 guidance is revenue growth of 3-4% with clear-aligner volume up ~6% and ASP flat to slightly down (Q2 2026 earnings reports). The base start of 4.3% sits at the top of that guidance — defensible only because the TTM base already reflects the H1 2026 cash recovery; it is not a conservative start. The bull (9.3%) and super-bull (16.3%) starts are above every recent print: they are re-acceleration cases (international double-digit volume growth annualizing, record scanner placements converting into cases) and are weighted only 20% / 10% for that reason. Default offsets −12/−5/0/+5/+12pp were kept; probabilities were shifted one notch bearish to 10/30/30/20/10 (from the 10/25/30/25/10 default) because guidance, the Q3 2026 guide (~+1.4% YoY revenue at the midpoint) and the OE_VOLATILE flag all point the same way. OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $149.00.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | -7.7% | 0.75 | Price war bites; NA starts fall; ASP declines compound | $25.45 | 4.37% |
| Bear | 30% | -0.7% | 0.90 | The FY2022-25 stall persists; volume growth eaten by ASP/mix | $40.96 | 5.83% |
| Base | 30% | 4.3% | 1.00 | Guidance-like growth; TTM cash conversion holds | $56.06 | 7.27% |
| Bull | 20% | 9.3% | 1.10 | International volume + scanner funnel re-accelerate growth | $75.84 | 9.10% |
| Super bull | 10% | 16.3% | 1.25 | Teen/international penetration drives a second growth leg | $114.75 | 12.41% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $58.29 (−60.9% vs price), IV@12% $77.44, IV@10% $98.79, weighted IRR 7.52%, base-case IRR 7.27%**
- **Tier by numbers: D** — and the whole band is D (bear tier D at 5.83%, bull tier D at 9.10%; even the super-bull scenario IRR of 12.41% only reaches C). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 4.26%, terminal value 18.7% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.51x, 9.6 months since FY end.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago): resolved by construction — the base is the TTM figure from ttm.py through Q2 2026, legs quoted above.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 2.5%/yr; CSV share CAGR −2.54%): already credited via the +2.54pp growth adjustment in the blend; not double-counted in the verdict.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share range over the last 5 years spans >3x): real and identified — OE/share ran $8.25 (FY2021, COVID-recovery demand peak) → $1.83 (FY2022, demand collapse with capex peaking at $291,900,000) → $5.93 / $5.99 / $4.20. Handled with the TTM base (which skips the distorted FY2025 print without reaching back to the peak) and by raising the bear weight to 30%.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2023, 2024): resolved — it is structural non-cash addbacks, not a one-off. In 2023 net income was $445,053,000 vs OCF $785,776,000; SBC $154,026,000 + D&A $142,401,000 = $296,427,000 of non-cash charges explains nearly all of the gap. In 2024 net income was $421,362,000 vs OCF $738,231,000; SBC $173,703,000 + D&A $145,034,000 = $318,737,000 against a gap of $316,869,000 — fully explained. The OCF-based conservative OE used throughout is unaffected.
- **DEBT_TAGS_BLANK** (no debt tag reports for the latest fiscal year): stated from the filing record — Align carries no borrowings: no debt tag is filed in any year of the history, FY2025 cash is $1,094,908,000 against total liabilities of $2,184,546,000 and equity of $4,049,147,000, and the only lease obligations are operating leases of $114,446,000 (financials_history.csv). Net debt is therefore not "unknown" in substance — the company is debt-free and net cash — but the engine correctly refuses to print a leverage ratio from blank tags, and none is quoted here.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.51x super-bear IV): real — the range is the honest output for a stalled grower whose re-acceleration case is speculative. Confidence is capped at medium, and the verdict is sized to the conservative end. It does not change the tier: every scenario, including super bull, prices below $149.00.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The method range is unusually tight for this sweep: the preliminary run on the normalized median base ($5.93/share, default probabilities) gave weighted IRR 7.35% and IV@15% $56.12; the final TTM-base run gives 7.52% and $58.29. Both are Tier D. The verdict does not depend on the base choice — it depends on the price, which capitalizes a growth re-acceleration the filings do not yet show.
- Quality is not the debate: debt-free, OE-positive 5/5 years, ROIC 13-17% through a stall, gross margin ~70%, buybacks shrinking the count ~2.5%/yr. The debate is growth: revenue has compounded at ~0.5%/yr since FY2021, guidance is 3-4%, and ASP is guided flat-to-down — the market price needs the bull case, the filings support the base case.
- Watch items: the FY2026 GAAP guide carries $90-100M of one-time charges (restructuring, accelerated depreciation, legal settlements) and a $38M UK VAT liability was recorded in Q2 2026 — if "one-time" charges recur, the TTM OE base is flattered and the bear case is the base case. Systems & Services revenue is guided down 6-8% in FY2026 on scanner mix shift to lower-priced units; management's claim is that placements widen the Invisalign funnel — Q2 2026 shipments (+7.4%) are early evidence for it, one quarter is not a trend.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 7.52% on the TTM base; the entire bear→bull band is D)
- Confidence: **Medium** (high on the filing-derived OE base and the debt-free balance sheet; the scenario spread is 4.51x, so no single growth path deserves high confidence)
- One-liner: High-quality, debt-free clear-aligner franchise, moat 5/10 — but growth has stalled at 3-4% guided and even the TTM base only yields 7.5% weighted IRR at $149; it clears 15% only below $58.29.
